title: IDCW vs SWP vs growth
objectives: Compare IDCW payout, SWP from growth and growth on who decides, predictability, tax and TDS.
Say which option fits regular income and which fits wealth building.
body_md:
Who decides the amount: the fund's trustees (IDCW payout), the investor (SWP from growth), nobody — no payout (growth). Predictability: IDCW is not guaranteed and can be cut or skipped; SWP is a fixed amount on a fixed date as long as units remain. What is taxed: the whole IDCW payout at the slab rate; only the gain inside each SWP withdrawal, as capital gains; nothing in growth until redemption. TDS: yes for IDCW above the yearly threshold; generally none for SWP for resident investors; none for growth.

|  | IDCW payout | SWP (from growth option) | Growth option |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Who decides the amount | The fund's trustees | The investor | — (no payout) |
| Predictability | Not guaranteed; can be cut or skipped | Fixed amount on a fixed date, as long as units remain | — |
| What is taxed | The whole payout, at the investor's slab rate | Only the gain inside each withdrawal, as capital gains | Nothing until the investor redeems |
| TDS | Yes, above the yearly threshold | Generally none for resident investors | None |
| Best for | Rare cases where the client accepts irregular payouts | Regular income: retirees, rent, fees | Long-term wealth building; no cash needed |

> **Talk-track:** “If you need income, let's set up an SWP: you choose the amount and the date, and you're taxed only on the gain part. IDCW gives the fund that choice, and the whole payout is taxed.”

> **Investor takeaway:** For regular income, an SWP usually beats IDCW on both control and tax.
example: Same ₹3 lakh a year out: IDCW taxes the whole ₹3 lakh; an SWP where 20% is gain taxes only about ₹60,000 as gain (illustrative; confirm with a CA).
say: SWP: you choose the amount and date; tax only on the gain part.
IDCW gives the fund the choice, and the whole payout is taxed.
never: IDCW is more predictable than an SWP.
Growth and IDCW options hold different portfolios.

check.q: Which option lets the investor choose a fixed monthly amount?
check.why: SWP from growth. The investor sets amount and date.

check.q: In an SWP, what is taxed?
check.why: Only the gain portion. Each withdrawal is part capital, part gain.

check.q: Which client is usually best served by an SWP?
o: A retiree needing fixed monthly income
check.why: A retiree needing fixed monthly income. Control and tax efficiency.
